Cell biology is the study of how cells work. Every living thing is made of cells, and the cell is
the smallest unit that can carry out the processes of life. Some organisms, such as bacteria, have only
one cell. Others, such as people, have trillions of cells.

Cells have parts called organelles. The nucleus holds the genes, which carry the instructions for the
cell. The mitochondria make the energy the cell needs. Ribosomes build the proteins that do most of the
work. Together, the organelles let the cell grow, repair itself, and divide.
